engines.name: Ventoy
engines.notes: Installs a boot manager once (Ventoy2Disk.sh -i -g), then images are copied on as plain files - never offered a writeMode: raw image (finding A11). Ventoy ships x86_64 binaries only, so this engine is hidden on arm64 rather than offered and broken (AGENTS.md §3).

engines.name: UEFI file copy
engines.notes: Copies a hybrid ISO's files onto a partition the caller already formatted and mounted - no install-to-device step, and no elevation, unlike every other engine here. Needs the target mounted, writable and FAT32; the guard runs in 'mounted-fat32-writable' mode for this engine instead of the usual 'unmounted' mode every other engine requires.

engines.name: WSL2 passthrough
engines.notes: Attaches the physical USB device into a WSL2 distro via usbipd-win so a real Linux dd is available on Windows; the only engine that can build a full-os (portable installed OS) stick.

engines.name: Native raw write
engines.notes: Block-for-block dd (or the platform's raw-disk-write equivalent). Works for both writeModes because a hybrid ISO is dd-writable too; this is the only non-interactive engine a writeMode: raw image (e.g. proxmox-ve) can ever be planned onto, together with wsl and rufus.

engines.name: Rufus
engines.notes: GUI-driven; AutoOS can only launch it and hand it the image, never script the write itself. interactive: true means this engine is unavailable under --dry-run and in the browser UI (plan B11/B12), which cannot drive a foreground dialog.
